metadata.title: Trading Day: AI trade unwind continues, but Nvidia beats

content.text:
By Jamie McGeever
ORLANDO, Florida, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The AI trade unwind continued on Tuesday, pushing global stocks lower ahead of Nvidia's quarterly earnings and as investors prepared for Anthropic's stock market launch later in the week, while solid US retail sales and hawkish comments from Fed officials kept alive expectations that interest rates are headed higher.
In my column today, I look at the red flags warning investors about a market top. Timing that top and exiting unscathed is virtually impossible, but investors won't have the excuse that they didn't see it coming.
Today's Key Reads
• Huang open to Nvidia return as scandal-hit chipmaker heads into results
• EXCLUSIVE-Trump's China data center curb advances despite Amazon, Google, Meta lobbying
• Nvidia turmoil marks the end of easy money for the AI trade
• Anthropic debuts to skeptics and dogged believers: Mike Dolan
• Deutsche Bank chair backs CEO after reports expose past lapses; Trump calls tax leak 'illegal'
• Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Japan -1.3%, Europe and UK both -1.8%, worst day since March. Nasdaq -0.7%, S&P 500 -1%, Dow -1.6%.SECTORS/SHARES: All 11 sectors in the S&P 500 fall. Financials -1.9%, comms services -1.3%. Nvidia +4% in choppy trade immediately after Q3 results. Salesforce -9.5%, Nike -6%, Broadcom +2.5%.FX: Dollar hits fresh 19-month high but ends the day lower. Chilean peso biggest gainer, +0.6%.BONDS: US yields down 2-4 bps across the curve.COMMODITIES/METALS: Oil edges higher, gold holds around one-year low $3,950/oz.
Today's Talking Points:
Saga
The soap opera around Nvidia took more plot twists on Tuesday. It was reported that the US Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the company, while earlier in the day former CEO Jensen Huang said he would be "honored" to return as CEO. This comes a day after Reuters reported that the company's board was not considering Huang's return.
Meanwhile, it was reported that his daughter, a senior director of product marketing at Nvidia, was closely involved in shaping the public defence of the company's ties to Singapore-based Megaspeed, while Huang has agreed to appear before Congress early next month. If that wasn't enough, Q3 results just landed and interim CEO Colette Kress hosted the earnings conference call.
"Several"
St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem wasn't beating around the bush on Tuesday: "The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve price stability in a timely manner." How many hikes does "several" cover? Probably four, in Musalem's view, because current policy is as much as a full percentage point below where it should be.
